title: Coefficient-compatible presentation of a rational split-node completion
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $S$ be a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak p\subset S$ be a maximal ideal such that the structure map $k\to S/\mathfrak p$ is an isomorphism. Put $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and give $\widehat A=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}A/\mathfrak m^r$ its induced $k$-algebra structure and maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose $\widehat A$ is isomorphic as a ring to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], without assuming the given ring isomorphism is $k$-linear. Then there exists an isomorphism $\widehat A\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ of complete local $k$-algebras, continuous in both directions for the powers of the respective maximal ideals. Equivalently, there is a continuous surjective $k$-algebra homomorphism $\pi:k[[u,v]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ with kernel $(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], whose restriction to constants is the structure map $k\to\widehat A$. Here the topology on $k[[u,v]]$ has the powers of $(u,v)$ as neighbourhoods of zero. This imposes no dimension hypothesis on $S$.

proof.text: Identify $F=S/\mathfrak p$ with $k$ through the given structure isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] (the identity extension $k/k$ is finite separable). It gives $n\ge2$ and a presentation $\widehat A\cong R=k[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ over $k$, with each $f_j\in(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Its coefficient section is the given map: a $k$-algebra section $F\to\widehat A$ with $F=k$ must send each $c$ to its structural image. Thus this presentation uses exactly the coefficient structure in the item, not the constants transported by the abstract ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C52, lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra, separable-residue-field clause and last paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Compose the underlying ring isomorphism $R\cong\widehat A$ with the assumed one to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. This verifies condition (c) of [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion] with $a=c=0$, $b=1$ and discriminant $1$. Its implication (c)$\Rightarrow$(b) gives a complete local $k$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat A\cong k[[x,y]]/(Q)$ for $Q=ax^2+bxy+cy^2$ with $\Delta=b^2-4ac\ne0$. The criterion assumes only the finite formal presentation, not a global dimension condition.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], both two-variable series rings are complete for their variable ideals. Use [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to define $\beta:k[[U,V]]\to k[[x,y]]$ by $U\mapsto L_1$, $V\mapsto L_2$, fixing constants; write $L_1=Ax+By$, $L_2=Cx+Dy$, $d=AD-BC\ne0$, and define $\gamma$ by $x\mapsto(DU-BV)/d$, $y\mapsto(-CU+AV)/d$. Its images also lie in the variable ideal, so the same universal property applies. The composites fix constants and variables, so uniqueness in that universal property makes them identities. The maps preserve the variable ideals and their powers, hence are continuous. Since $\beta(UV)=Q$, they send the principal ideals $(UV)$ and $(Q)$ onto each other. The maps on cosets $[h]\mapsto[\beta(h)]$ and $[g]\mapsto[\gamma(g)]$ are well-defined inverse $k$-algebra maps. Combining this quotient isomorphism with Step 2 gives $e:k[[U,V]]/(UV)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat A$.

source.place: Tag 0C49, lemma-nodal-algebraic, split quadratic coordinates; power-series substitution as in algebra.tex Tag 032A, theorem-cohen-structure-theorem.

proof.text: A ring isomorphism between local rings sends their unique maximal ideals onto each other, and hence also their powers. Thus $e$ and $e^{-1}$ are continuous for the stipulated maximal-ideal-adic topologies. By [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], the quotient map $q:k[[U,V]]\to k[[U,V]]/(UV)$ is a surjective $k$-algebra map with kernel $(UV)$. Put $\pi=e\circ q$. Its kernel is $(UV)$ since $e$ is injective, it is surjective, and it fixes the structural constants since both factors are $k$-linear. The quotient map sends $(U,V)^r$ into the $r$th power of the quotient maximal ideal, so $\pi$ is continuous. This proves both formulations.
